quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Release the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the ignition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal. Steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

questions.question: True or False: Your speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you brake.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Speed affects stopping distance. As you drive faster, your vehicle needs more distance to stop. Stay far behind other vehicles when driving at high speeds.

questions.question: When a school bus has red flashing lights, you must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: Stay stopped until the red lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus begins moving again.

questions.question: In bad weather, how far back should you stay from the car ahead?

options.text: Four seconds.
Three seconds.
Two seconds.
One second.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of distance between your vehicle and others in poor weather. This gives you more time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: What do round signs mean?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn of a railroad crossing ahead. Drive carefully and watch for trains.

questions.question: What is the term for the amount of alcohol in your blood?

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter.
Only use the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot. Check several times and watch traffic in front of you and in the next lane.

questions.question: If you stop on the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off all lights.
Use parking lights only.
Use headlights only.
Turn on emergency flashers and leave low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and leave low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beam headlights on. Make sure other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not pass.
Do not enter.
No turn on red.
Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead. The road will split into two separate one-way roads. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: If you are in a collision, what should you do about injured people?

options.text: Move them far away from the road.
Move them where they want to go.
Tell them they are fine and do not need help.
Do not move them unless you must to protect them from danger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless you must to protect them from danger.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless necessary to keep them safe from fire or other dangers. Keep them lying or sitting down until medical help arrives.

questions.question: When a school bus stops ahead to pick up or drop off children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children have left the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes back.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes back.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops with flashing red lights and a stop arm out, you must stop. Do not move until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is back. Even after the bus moves, wait until you are sure no children are crossing in front of you.

questions.question: At a flashing red light, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also coming.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic pass, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: A green arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You can go like a regular green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may go only if there is also a circular green light.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go like a regular green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means the same as a regular green light. Traffic in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: You should always drive:

options.text: At the same speed as the cars around you.
At the speed limit.
At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should depend on road conditions, weather, and the speed limit. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Drive slower when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of the road. To prevent it in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep the same speed.
Slow down.
Move to the road's shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the pavement is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The divided highway is ending.
The divided highway is starting.
The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a divided highway is coming. Stay to the right of the median divider.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between lanes is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. You may cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane if you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle to your right anymore.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back to your lane after passing, make sure you are far enough from the other vehicle. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return safely.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your car.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have big blind spots on each side. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.
